summary: Final candidate is an explicitly new, untested bridge: altered-template transcription could produce a species X that preferentially adsorbs to an internal boundary and alters its interfacial free energy, potentially affecting cavity persistence. The phase diagram is P (surrounding RNA-rich phase) | X (hypothetical adsorbed or, in the stronger subcase, macroscopic intervening phase) | V (RNA-poor cavity). For a macroscopic intervening X phase, interfacial replacement gives Delta gamma = gamma_PX + gamma_XV - gamma_PV = -S_X, where S_X = gamma_PV - gamma_PX - gamma_XV. Thus S_X >= 0 conditionally favors that replacement in interfacial free energy. This is dimensional energy/area bookkeeping, not a sourced or measured result here; it cannot be applied to molecular adsorption without a third-phase layer. E01 shows B mean segmented area fraction rising 0.01381 to 0.08918 over 0-24 h and A falling to about 0.0045, but has two independent preparations and nested fields. E02 links template-fraction groups to a separate endpoint, not causally or temporally. E03 lacks within-droplet cavity-state tracks. E04 has bulk tie-line RNA concentrations but no cavity mapping, phase volumes, or B time series. E05 DNA read fractions do not specify RNA identity or abundance. Search S-L1 returned an abstract with broad associative/segregative biomacromolecule phase-transition context only; S-R1 returned zero sources; S-L2 returned zero eligible sources, with five exclusions. No retrieved result supports RNA internal-boundary wetting or the generic formula. No computation was run.

final.actual_derivation_or_computation: No numerical computation was run. Conditional derivation: gamma_PV is the interfacial cost per area before insertion of a macroscopic X layer; after insertion the cost is gamma_PX + gamma_XV. Therefore Delta gamma = gamma_PX + gamma_XV - gamma_PV = -S_X. All terms have energy/area units; S_X >= 0 favors this replacement under the assumed equilibrium geometry.

Bulk demixing does not require this pattern, though incidental enrichment is possible, so enrichment is supportive but not exclusive or causal proof.
